Unstated gender: mental_state answer says 'what the narrator says she couldn't tell'; the observer is never gendered; Minor fidelity: the mother speaks for Rafiq ('He doesn't feel like a hug today'); the child never practises saying no himself | suggested: Use 'the narrator' / 'they'; optionally let Rafiq say 'No hug' before Jahnavi offers the high-five.

Muddled kinship: 'A neighbour... Maria, was visiting' then 'the grandmother said, "Give Dadi a kiss"' - whose Dadi, and whom is Maria visiting, is unclear; Observer overclaims inner state: 'Maria's choice made her comfortable' (recipe: observer does not know for sure); Name reuse: Dilnaz is the mother in 2216 v2 and the child here | suggested: Make it 'Dilnaz's Dadi' at Maria's own home, and change the last line to 'she looked easier after that'.

Leak: application answer copies description wording 'feels wrong or someone asks for secrecy' (6-word run); Sabina's hands 'went still' and she asks about secrets; the counsellor just says 'Good.' - no gentle private check-in, which weakens the trusted-adult model; Absolute rule 'Nobody else may touch the parts of your body that are private' with no age-appropriate note (e.g. a parent helping at bath time or a doctor with a parent there) | suggested: Reword the application answer; add one line of the counsellor quietly telling Sabina she can come and talk any time; optionally add the caregiver/doctor-with-parent exception in child words.

Safeguarding response: after 'Let's find someone who can help you both right now' the adult 'went to bring the head teacher', leaving the disclosing child alone; Missing reassurance that it is not the child's fault | suggested: Adult stays with Shankar and Lokesh and asks another staff member to fetch the head teacher; add 'You did the right thing telling. It's not your fault.'

Unstated gender: perspective 'She might find it charming' for the nurse; 'the card that his uncle had shown him' appears with no set-up (the shared signal is never shown being agreed); Name reuse: Thomas and Chinmay are father and son in 2446 v1, nephew and uncle here | suggested: Use 'the nurse'/'they'; add one line of Chinmay showing the quiet-voice card outside.

Disclosure scene with no trusted adult responding: Ayo 'heard whispers and smiled' and is nearby, but the passage ends with the boys holding hands and a plan to tell 'your mum' later; Mental_state answer says 'he told Emeka in a low voice'; passage only says 'Liam grew quiet' | suggested: End with the boys going to Ayo, who kneels, listens calmly, thanks Liam and says she will make sure his mum knows tonight.

REJECT: rewrite this record. Safety/teaches wrong response: a 5-year-old trails off about 'the bruise on his arm' with 'he said...' and pulls his sleeve down; the note ends 'he may simply have lost the word' and only asks the counsellor to 'keep an eye on him' - an injury plus a possible disclosure should be recorded and passed to the school's safeguarding lead the same day; Loads the row: the description's neutral 'lost the words' reading becomes a dismissal of an abuse cue; Unstated gender: answers call Mridul 'him'/'He'; the passage never genders the teacher | suggested: Regenerate with a non-injury topic (e.g. trailing off about a broken toy or a weekend trip) so the alternative readings stay neutral; or, if the bruise stays, the teacher writes down Sumit's exact words and reports to the designated safeguarding lead today, without questioning him further.

Unstated gender: literal answer 'She was sitting at the back of the library'; the observer is never gendered; Ambiguous: 'Farida said "Shh, shh," softly, stroking her arm' - Farida is soothing a stranger's toddler, or Nandini? | suggested: Answer 'The narrator was sitting...'; make it 'the toddler's father said shh softly' or clarify whose arm.

Late name insertion reads unnaturally: 'Beta, come sit. Madhav here has a story' - the speaker refers to himself in the third person; Unclear event: 'the teacher's chair broke... He had sat on it first, you see'; Literal Q invents 'the teacher's room'; passage says only 'the teacher's chair'; Emoji '🙂' ends a spoken story - decoration, not something typed | suggested: Open with 'Beta, come sit. I'm your Madhav Dada, and this is from my school days in Nashik.'; make it 'Shankar had been sitting on it when it broke'; fix the literal Q; drop the emoji.

Unstated gender: answers and grounding use 'he'/'him' for Gurpreet (a name used for both genders; the passage has no pronoun); Fidelity partial: description's 'ask repeated questions' and 'honest answers' are not shown (Mummy asks; the child never asks); Name reads naturally ('I'm Gurpreet, and when my grandfather died I was ten') - no issue there | suggested: Use 'Gurpreet' / 'they' in answers and grounding; add one line of Gurpreet asking the same question again and Mummy answering honestly.

Unstated gender: mental_state 'He felt bad' and grounding 'wrinkles his nose' for Nilesh; the narrator is never gendered; Name insertion 'I'm Nilesh, and I don't like it when Tarun comes to lunch' reads naturally | suggested: Use 'Nilesh' or 'the child' in answers and grounding.

Sensitive (grief) passage ends with an emoji in narration: '...sleepy and comfortable." 🤍' - the rule allows at most one gentle emoji, in an answer only | suggested: Remove the emoji from the passage (optionally move 🤍 to the perspective answer).

Garbled perspective Q: 'How might Payal have felt when Indu was thought to hate them?'; Application answer repeats the name awkwardly: 'Payal can ask, as Payal suggests' | suggested: Ask 'How might Payal have felt on learning Indu was only cold?'; tidy the application answer.
